# Proposing a content edit (note change)

Any time you change the **notes** in a quartet — fix a wrong pitch, a rhythm, an
accidental — use this process so the change is previewed and explained before it
lands. The point is that a reviewer can *see* what moved without rebuilding
anything, and there's a written record of why.

Each change lives in its own folder under `changes/<slug>/`:

```
changes/op32-4-mvt2-bar3/
  change.patch   # the exact edit (a unified diff of the note file)
  NOTES.md       # what changed, why, with before/after images
  *-before.png   # generated by the preview tool
  *-after.png
```

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `tools/preview-music-change.sh` | Renders score + affected part before/after a patch, finds the changed page(s), writes tight before/after PNGs. Never touches your sources. |
| `tools/crop_changed.py` | Helper: locates the changed band between two page rasters (pure stdlib). |
| `tools/open-change-pr.sh` | Turnkey: branch → apply patch → rebuild → commit → push → open a PR with the images embedded. |

Requirements: `lilypond`, `pdftoppm` (poppler), `python3`, and `gh` (for the PR).

## Step by step

### 1. Make the edit and capture it as a patch

Edit the note file, diff it, then restore it (the patch is the proposal; it gets
applied later by the PR step):

```bash
slug=op32-4-mvt2-bar3
mkdir -p changes/$slug
# ... edit Op32-4/04-Vc-2.ily in your editor ...
git diff -- Op32-4/04-Vc-2.ily > changes/$slug/change.patch
git restore Op32-4/04-Vc-2.ily
```

**Mind relative octaves.** Note files are in `\relative` mode, so a pitch is read
relative to the one before it. Changing a note can shift the octave of the *next*
note — if so, add a `'` (up) or `,` (down) to the following note to pin it. The
preview will show any unintended octave jump immediately.

**Line endings.** Some quartets (Op32/Op33) use CRLF. Keep them: edit in place
rather than rewriting the file, so the patch touches only the lines you mean to.

### 2. Preview it

```bash
tools/preview-music-change.sh Op32-4 changes/$slug/change.patch changes/$slug
```

This writes `Score-before/after.png` (full page, for harmonic context) and
`<Part>-before/after.png` (cropped to the changed system, with every bar
numbered) into the change folder, plus a `preview-summary.md` you can paste from.
Check that **only** the bars you intended moved.

### 3. Explain it

Write `changes/$slug/NOTES.md`: the quartet/movement/bar, the source or authority
for the correction, what the patch changes (and any octave-compensation), and the
before/after images. See `changes/op32-4-mvt2-bar3/NOTES.md` for the template.

### 4. Open the PR

```bash
tools/open-change-pr.sh $slug Op32-4
```

It creates a branch, applies the patch, runs `make Op32-4` to confirm it still
engraves, commits the source edit together with the change folder (patch, notes,
images), pushes, and opens a PR whose body embeds the before/after images. Review
and merge on GitHub.

To do it by hand instead, the equivalent is: `git switch -c change/$slug`,
`patch Op32-4/04-Vc-2.ily < changes/$slug/change.patch`, `make Op32-4`,
`git add Op32-4 changes/$slug && git commit`, `git push -u origin change/$slug`,
`gh pr create`.
